div.head: III Eg 7
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe tyhtbysig sý ⁊ folce ungetriwe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge, þonne sceawie man of ðam gemote þa þe him toridan, ⁊ finde him þonne gyt borh, gyf he mæge.
⁊ se þe tihtbysig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemót forbuge ðriwa, þonne sceapige mon of þam gemote ða ðe him tórídon, ⁊ finde him þonne gyt borh, gyf he mæge.
And se þe tihtbisig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge þrywa, þonne scifte man of þam gemote ða ðe him toridan, ⁊ finde þonne git borh, gif he mæge.
⁊ se ðe tyhtbysig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge þrywa, þonne scawie man of þam gemote þa ðe him tóridan, ⁊ finde þonne gyt borh, gif he mæge.
Et qui fuerit accusationibus infamatus et populo incredibilis et hec placita declinauerit, uideatur de (ipso) placito qui mittantur ad eum, et inueniat etiam tunc sibi fideiussores, si possit.
[Be tyhtbysigum.] ⁊ se þe tihtbisig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge þrywa, þonne scifte man of þam gemote ða ðe him toridan, ⁊ finde þonne git borh, gif he mæge.
And se ðe tyhtbysig sy and folce ungetriwe and þas gemot forbuge þriwa, þonne sceawie man of ðam gemote þa þe him to ridan. And finde him þonne gyt borh, gyf he mæge.

(Von oft Bescholtenen. Ld) Und wer oft bescholten ist und der Allgemeinheit Vertrauens unwürdig [gilt] und diese Gerichtsversammlungen dreimal (fehlt G Qu.) vermeidet: dann möge man aus der Gerichtsversammlung die [Männer] aussuchen (abordnen D), welche zu ihm ziehen sollen, und er mag sich [auch] dann noch Bürgschaft finden, wenn er kann.

(Of those often accused. Ld) And whoever is often accused and [held] untrustworthy by the people and avoids these court-meetings three times (lacking in G, Qu.): then let [men] be chosen (appointed, D) from the court-meeting to ride to him, and let him [even] then still find himself a surety, if he can.

And if anyone who has a bad reputation and is unworthy of public confidence fails to attend the court-meetings three times, men shall be chosen from the meeting who shall ride to him, and he may then still find a surety, if he can.

And he who is frequently accused and is unworthy of the people’s trust, and who fails to attend these meetings—then men are to be chosen from the meeting to ride to him; and he may still provide a surety, if he can.

And if anyone who is disreputable or deemed untrustworthy by the community fails to attend public meetings three times, then let three men of that meeting be chosen to ride to him. And he may still find a surety, if he can.

Vielleicht (bestimmt begrenzter als bloss ‘Öffentlichkeit’) die Gerichtsgemeinde, denn II Cn 30 setzt hundred dafür. Jedenfalls nicht etwa das Volk des ganzen Landes als Staat oder gar als dessen höchster Machtfaktor

Perhaps (more narrowly defined than mere ‘public’) the community of the court, since II Cn 30 puts hundred for it. At any rate not, say, the people of the whole country as the state, or even as its highest power
Mehrmalige Gerichtsversäumnisse (s. d. Gl 3) sind gemeint laut des Plurals þas und des folgenden þonne gyt; also stand þrywa in Eg's Archetyp wie in der Quelle und im Benutzer

Repeated defaults of attendance at court (see that word in Gl 3) are meant, according to the plural þas and the following þonne gyt; so þrywa stood in Eg’s archetype, as in the source and in the borrower
‘vierten’ Cnut. Auch in II As 20, 1 tritt der Zwang erst ein, wenn die (bei vierter Tagung) nach drei Malen fällige Strafzahlung ausblieb
‘fourth’ Cnut. In II As 20, 1 too, compulsion begins only when the fine due after three times (at the fourth session) has not been paid

Q wählt von sceawic die hier unpassende Bed. Dafür ist A's sceapige, auch in II Cn 25, nur Schreibfehler, vielleicht erklärbar aus Mittelengl. schapie (Mayhew and Skeat) ‘adiudicet, bestimme’; vielleicht daher übs. Cons Cn: annominentur. D führt ein Lehnwort aus Nordischem ein.—Der Vollstrecker ist nicht der Herr, sondern eine Kommission des Gerichts; s. d. Gl 20e; Bürgschaft 6f.

Q chooses the meaning of sceawic that is unsuitable here. A’s sceapige in its place, also in II Cn 25, is merely a scribal error, perhaps explicable from Middle English schapie (Mayhew and Skeat) ‘adiudicet, determine’; perhaps hence Cons Cn translates annominentur. D introduces a loan-word from Norse. — The executor is not the lord but a commission of the court; see that word in Gl 20e; Bürgschaft 6f.
In view of II Cn. 30 ungetreowe þam hundrede, Liebermann takes this to refer simply to the members of the court, not to the public at large.
scifte (D) is a Scandinavian loan word.
